subject: Physics
cards: AQA-8463.DIRECT_POTENTIAL_DIFFERENCE

What is meant by ‘direct potential difference’?

[1 mark]

polarity of the potential difference doesn’t change
Also accept: direction of the potential difference doesn’t change
AQA-8463.DIRECT_CURRENT

What is meant by direct current?

[1 mark]
current that is always in the same direction
AQA-8463.ZERO_ERROR

The ammeter used had a zero error. What is meant by a zero error?

[1 mark]
ammeter displays a reading when not connected (to a circuit)
AQA-8463.ISOTOPES

Describe what is meant by ‘isotopes’ of an element.

[2 marks]

• (atoms of an element with) the same number of protons
• but a different number of neutrons
Also accept: same atomic number
Also accept: different mass number
Ignore: number of electrons
AQA-8463.CENTRE_OF_MASS

What is meant by ‘centre of mass’?

[1 mark]

• the point from which weight may be considered to act
• or
• the point where the mass appears to be concentrated
Also accept: the point through which the line of action of the weight acts
Also accept: the point at which the mass is concentrated
AQA-8463.RED-SHIFT

Describe what is meant by red-shift.

[2 marks]

• the (observed) increase in wavelength (of light from galaxies)
• as galaxies move away from us
Ignore: light waves are stretched
AQA-8463.MOMENTUM_IS_CONSERVED

What is meant by ‘momentum is conserved’?

[1 mark]

(total) momentum before = (total) momentum after
Also accept: (total) momentum stays the same
AQA-8463.HALF-LIFE

What is meant by ‘half-life’?

[1 mark]
the time it takes for the count rate of a sample to halve
AQA-8463.RANDOM_NATURE_OF_RADIOACTIVE_DECAY

What is meant by the ‘random nature of radioactive decay’?

[1 mark]

• can’t predict which nucleus will decay next
• or
• can’t predict when a (particular) nucleus will decay
AQA-8463.MOMENT_OF_A_FORCE

What is meant by the ‘moment’ of a force?

[1 mark]
the turning effect of the force
AQA-8463.CLOSED_SYSTEM

What is meant by a ‘closed system’?

[1 mark]

• the total amount of energy (of the bumper car and barrier) remains constant.
• or
• total momentum (of bumper car and barrier) before collision equals total momentum (of bumper car and barrier) after collision
• or
• the resultant external force acting (on the system) is zero
Also accept: there are no external forces (acting on the system)
AQA-8463.R_4_1_1_FUSION_REACTOR_WALLS

The fusion reaction releases large amounts of energy. The fusion reaction takes place in a reactor. Explain why the walls of the reactor should be made from a material with a very high specific heat capacity.

[2 marks]

• (a large amount of energy transferred) causes a small temperature increase of the walls / material
• (therefore) the walls of the reactor should not reach melting point
Also accept: (therefore) the walls of the reactor should not melt
AQA-8463.R_4_2_5_CLOTH_BECOMES_POSITIVE

A student rubbed a plastic rod with a cloth. The rod became negatively charged and the cloth became positively charged. Explain why the cloth became positively charged.

[3 marks]

• electrons transferred from the cloth (to the rod)
• electrons are negatively charged
• (so) there are more positive charges than negative charges on the cloth
Not accepted: any mention of transfer of positive charge scores 0
Not accepted: any mention of positive electrons scores 0
Ignore: more protons than electrons unqualified
AQA-8463.R_4_2_5_SPARK_TO_EARTHED_CONDUCTOR

A negatively charged rod is held near an earthed conductor. Explain why a spark jumps between the negatively charged rod and the earthed conductor.

[3 marks]

• the (large) potential difference between the two objects
• (causes negative) electrons / charges to move (through the air)
• (from the rod) to the conductor
Also accept: (strong) electric field causes breakdown of air
Also accept: there is a current in the air (between the two objects)
Not accepted: earthed conductor is positively charged
AQA-8463.R_4_4_4_NUCLEAR_FUSION_ENERGY_RELEASE

Explain how nuclear fusion releases energy.

[3 marks]

• light(er) nuclei fuse
• to form heavier nuclei / elements
• some of the mass (of the nuclei) is converted into energy (of radiation)
Also accept: hydrogen nuclei fuse
Also accept: to form helium nuclei
Ignore: bonding / colliding
AQA-8463.R_4_4_1_CARBON_14_VS_CARBON_12

Carbon-14 and carbon-12 are isotopes of carbon. Compare the structure of an atom of carbon-14 with the structure of an atom of carbon-12.

[3 marks]

Similarities:
• same number of protons
• or
• same atomic number
• same number of electrons
Difference:
• different number of neutrons
• or
• different mass number
Also accept: both atoms / nuclei contain 6 protons
Also accept: carbon-12 has 6 neutrons and carbon-14 has 8 neutrons
AQA-8463.R_4_4_1_ELECTRON_MOVES_BETWEEN_ENERGY_LEVELS

Explain how an electron can move up and down between energy levels in an atom.

[2 marks]

• to move to a higher energy level an electron absorbs energy from electromagnetic radiation
• to move to a lower energy level an electron emits energy in the form of electromagnetic radiation
Also accept: absorbs energy by collision with another electron
Also accept: EM radiation for electromagnetic radiation
Also accept: if no other mark scored allow 1 mark for an electron changes energy level by emitting or absorbing electromagnetic radiation
AQA-8463.R_4_4_2_WORKER_CLOSE_TO_DETECTOR

Workers in nuclear power stations are monitored to check the radiation they emit. A worker stands 1 cm away from a radiation detector. The amount of radiation the worker emits is recorded. Explain why the worker needs to stand close to the radiation detector.

[2 marks]

• some radioactive materials emit alpha radiation
• which has a (very) short range (in air)
Also accept: weakly penetrating for short range (in air)
AQA-8463.R_4_4_2_POLONIUM_ACTIVITY_HALF_LIFE

A sample of polonium contains equal numbers of polonium-209 atoms and polonium-210 atoms. Polonium-209 has a half-life of 125 years. Polonium-210 has a half-life of 138 days. Explain how the activity of polonium-209 compares with the activity of polonium-210 in this sample.

[2 marks]

• polonium-209 has a lower **activity** than polonium-210
• (because polonium-209) has a longer half-life
Ignore: description of rate of decay
AQA-8463.R_4_5_6_VELOCITY_VS_SPEED

An aircraft travels at a constant velocity. How is the velocity of the aircraft different to the speed of the aircraft?

[1 mark]

velocity includes direction
Also accept: velocity is a vector (quantity) and speed is a scalar (quantity)
AQA-8463.R_4_5_6_INERTIA_DEFINITION

What is inertia?

[1 mark]

the tendency of an object to continue in its state of rest or motion
Also accept: how difficult it is to change the velocity of an object
AQA-8463.R_4_5_6_MASS_AND_MAXIMUM_ACCELERATION

A car manufacturer makes two cars, X and Y. The cars are identical, apart from their mass. Car X has a greater mass than car Y. How does the maximum acceleration of car X compare with the maximum acceleration of car Y?

[1 mark]
car **X** has a smaller maximum acceleration (than car **Y**)
AQA-8463.R_4_5_6_BRAKES_GET_HOT

Explain why braking causes an increase in the temperature of the brakes.

[2 marks]

• work is done by friction (in the brakes)
• (some of the kinetic) energy (of the vehicle) is transferred as thermal energy (in the brakes)
Ignore: friction alone
AQA-8463.R_4_5_6_AIR_BAGS_REDUCE_INJURY

Cars have air bags that inflate to protect the driver if the car stops very suddenly. Explain how air bags reduce the chance of injury to the driver.

[3 marks]

• increases the time taken (for the driver to come to a stop)
• (so) the rate of change of momentum decreases
• or
• the deceleration / acceleration of the driver is less
• (so) the force (on the driver) is reduced
Also accept: for MP1 **and** MP2 the change of momentum is the same but over a greater time
AQA-8463.R_4_6_2_VISIBLE_LIGHT_NOT_ABSORBED_BY_OZONE

The Sun emits visible light. A student concludes that visible light is not absorbed by the ozone layer. Give one piece of evidence that shows the student’s conclusion is correct.

[1 mark]

our eyes detect visible light
Also accept: it would be dark all the time
Also accept: specific effect ie plants couldn’t grow
AQA-8463.R_4_8_1_FEW_PEOPLE_VISIT_ISS

Very few people have been to the International Space Station. Suggest one reason why very few people have been to the International Space Station.

[1 mark]

• expensive
• or
• dangerous
Also accept: difficult to get to
Also accept: few opportunities
Also accept: only trained astronauts can go
AQA-8463.R_4_2_4_HIGH_PD_TRANSMISSION

Explain the advantage of transmitting electricity at a very high potential difference.

[3 marks]

• (very high p.d. means) very low currents
• which means less (thermal) energy is transferred to surroundings
• which increases the efficiency of power transmission
Also accept: less power loss in cables
AQA-8463.R_4_3_3_MORE_AIR_PRESSURE

When the tyre is at the correct pressure, pumping more air into the tyre causes the pressure to increase further. The volume and temperature of the air in the tyre do not change. Explain why the pressure increases as more air is pumped into the tyre.

[2 marks]

• more (air) particles (in the tyre)
• greater number of collisions with tyre (walls) per second
Also accept: collisions with tyre (walls) are more frequent
Also accept: greater rate of collisions with tyre (walls)
Not accepted: MP2 if linked to an increased air temperature or increased speed / Ek of particles
Ignore: greater force per m2
AQA-8463.R_4_3_3_TEMPERATURE_GAS_PRESSURE

The air pressure in a car tyre changes if the temperature of the air in the tyre increases. Explain why.

[4 marks]

• (as temperature increases the) air particles have greater (mean) kinetic energy
• (so) more collisions with tyre (walls) per second
• (and) greater force in each collision
• greater (mean) force per square metre causes greater pressure (on wall of tyre)
Also accept: particles move with greater speeds (on average)
Also accept: collisions with tyre (walls) are more frequent
Also accept: greater rate of collisions with tyre (walls)
Also accept: greater rate of change of momentum in each collision
Also accept: ‘on a given area’ for ‘per square metre’
AQA-8463.R_4_3_3_VOLUME_DECREASE_PRESSURE

A student investigated how the pressure in a fixed mass of air varies with the volume of the air. When the plunger was pushed slowly into the syringe, the pressure in the syringe increased. The temperature of the air remained constant. Explain why the pressure increased.

[3 marks]

• (air) particles are closer together
• (so) frequency of collision between air particles and syringe walls increased
• larger (total) force on a smaller (surface) area
Also accept: larger force per unit area
Also accept: if no other marks score allow 1 mark for pressure increases because volume decreases and pV = constant
Not accepted: MP2 if linked to an increase in kinetic energy
Ignore: reference to kinetic energy of particles
Ignore: reference to concentration of air particles
AQA-8463.R_4_5_2_ELECTRIC_CAR_RANGE

The battery in an electric car needs to be recharged. Suggest two factors that affect the distance an electric car can travel before the battery needs to be recharged.

[2 marks]

any **two** from:
• capacity of the battery
• speed
• mass / weight
• uphill / downhill
• stopping at traffic lights
• condition of the road
• (air) temperature
• (incorrect) tyre pressure
• streamlining of the car
Also accept: energy/charge stored in battery
Also accept: efficiency of battery
Also accept: terrain
Also accept: efficiency of engine
Also accept: anything that would use charge from the battery or anything that will reduce the energy stored
Ignore: size of the battery
Ignore: ‘the road’ only
Ignore: ‘weather’ only
AQA-8463.R_4_7_1_INDUCED_MAGNET

What is an induced magnet?

[1 mark]

• an induced magnet is a material that becomes a magnet when it is placed in a magnetic field
• or
• an induced magnet loses most / all of its magnetism (quickly) when removed from a magnetic field
Also accept: ‘when close to another magnet’ for ‘when it is placed in a magnetic field’
Also accept: ‘no magnets are nearby’ for ‘removed from a magnetic field’
Not accepted: ‘temporary magnet’ alone is insufficient
AQA-8463.R_4_7_2_FIELD_LINE_ARROWS

What do the arrows on the magnetic field lines represent?

[1 mark]
direction (of the magnetic field)
AQA-8463.R_4_7_2_LOUDSPEAKER_EFFECT

A student made a moving-coil loudspeaker. What is the name of the effect used by the moving-coil loudspeaker to produce sound waves?

[1 mark]
motor (effect)
AQA-8463.R_4_1_3_COAL_ENVIRONMENT

Explain one environmental problem caused when electricity is generated by burning coal.

[2 marks]

• carbon dioxide released
• causing global warming
• OR
• particulates released
• causing global dimming
• OR
• sulfur dioxide released
• causing acid rain
Also accept: CO2
Also accept: climate change
Also accept: named consequence of global warming
Also accept: greenhouse effect
Also accept: SO2
Not accepted: greenhouse gases is insufficient
Not accepted: carbon emissions is insufficient
Not accepted: air pollution is insufficient
AQA-8463.R_4_1_3_RENEWABLE_NONRENEWABLE

Describe the difference between renewable energy resources and non-renewable energy resources.

[2 marks]

• renewable: (an energy resource that is) replenished (as it is used)
• non-renewable: (an energy resource that is) finite
Also accept: replaced for replenished
Also accept: limited supply
Ignore: has an infinite supply
Ignore: not running out
Ignore: sustainable
Ignore: running out
Ignore: won’t last forever
AQA-8463.R_4_1_2_EFFICIENT_DEVICES

In most homes in the UK there are many different electrical devices. Explain why people should be encouraged to use energy efficient electrical devices.

[2 marks]

• more efficient devices waste less energy
• or
• more efficient devices need a lower energy input (for the same energy output)
• which would minimise the electricity / energy demand
• or
• which would minimise the environmental impact from (fossil fuel) electricity generation
Also accept: less electricity needs to be generated
Also accept: lower energy / electricity bill
Also accept: examples of environmental impact e.g. lower CO2 emissions
Ignore: use less electricity
Ignore: ‘better for the environment’ unless qualified
Ignore: answers that discuss ‘saving energy’ unless qualified
Ignore: answers that discuss alternative methods of generating electricity
AQA-8463.R_4_1_2_OILING_EFFICIENCY

Some of the energy from the wind used to rotate a wind turbine is wasted. An engineer oils the mechanical parts of a wind turbine. Explain how oiling would affect the efficiency of the wind turbine.

[3 marks]

• the efficiency would increase
• because the percentage / proportion / amount of energy usefully transferred would increase
• or
• because the percentage / proportion / amount of energy wasted would decrease
• (because) less (work is done against) friction
Also accept: less energy wasted
Ignore: more electricity generated
AQA-8463.R_4_1_3_WIND_NOT_MEET_DEMAND

On one day the demand for electricity in the UK was 34 000 MW. Suggest two reasons why wind power was not able to meet this demand.

[2 marks]

any **2** from:
• wind is unreliable
• wind turbines don’t turn when the wind is too strong/weak
• there are not enough wind turbines (in the UK)
Also accept: it was not windy (on that day)
Also accept: some wind turbines may be offline for maintenance
Also accept: energy from wind may not be enough (to generate 34 000 MW)
Ignore: weather conditions unqualified
AQA-8463.R_4_1_1_PUMPED_WATER_STORE

Which energy store increases when water is pumped uphill into a reservoir?

[1 mark]

gravitational potential (energy)
Also accept: Ep / GPE
Also accept: kinetic / Ek
AQA-8463.R_4_1_1_WATER_HEATED_STORE

Which energy store increases when water is heated?

[1 mark]

• thermal / internal (energy)
• or
• kinetic (energy of the water particles)
Also accept: Ek
Ignore: heat
AQA-8463.R_4_1_1_SHC_REDUCE_ENERGY_LOSS

A student determined the specific heat capacity of water. One source of error in the experiment was energy loss to the surroundings. Suggest one change to the apparatus to reduce energy loss to the surroundings.

[1 mark]

• insulate the beaker of water
• or
• add a lid
Also accept: named insulation
Also accept: use an insulating cup
Also accept: eg plastic cup
AQA-8463.R_4_2_1_VARY_LED_PD

A student investigated how the current in an LED varies with the potential difference across the LED. Give one way the student could have varied the potential difference across the LED.

[1 mark]

any **one** from:
• change the resistance of the variable resistor
• change the number of cells in the battery
• change the potential difference of the power supply / pack
• add additional resistors / components to the circuit
Also accept: use the variable resistor
Also accept: add another battery
Also accept: use a battery with a higher / lower potential difference
AQA-8463.R_4_2_1_CELL_NOT_HAZARD

A student investigated how the length of a wire affects the resistance of the wire at constant temperature. The student used a cell that had a potential difference of 1.50 V. Explain why the cell was not an electrical hazard to the student in the investigation.

[2 marks]

• potential difference is (very) low
• (so) no risk of electric shock
• or
• (so) no risk of electrocution
Also accept: less risk of electric shock
Also accept: so wire won’t melt
Also accept: so wire won’t get hot
AQA-8463.R_4_6_1_REPEAT_AND_MEAN

What is the advantage of repeating measurements and calculating a mean?

[1 mark]

to reduce the effect of random errors
Also accept: gives a more accurate mean
Ignore: reference to anomalous results
Ignore: measurements are more accurate
AQA-8463.R_4_6_1_WIDE_RAY

A student investigated the refraction of light at the boundary between air and glass. The ray of light from the ray box should be as narrow as possible. Explain why using a wider ray would give less accurate results than using a narrower ray.

[2 marks]

• it is harder to judge where the centre of a wider ray is
• causing a larger uncertainty (in the measurements)
Also accept: increasing random errors (in the measurements)
AQA-8463.R_4_1_3_MORE_CO2_ELECTRIC_CAR

Manufacturing a car produces carbon dioxide. Some energy resources emit carbon dioxide when used to generate electricity. The battery-powered electric car does not emit carbon dioxide as it is driven. Explain why more carbon dioxide is produced as the distance travelled by the electric car increases.

[2 marks]

• the car / battery needs (re)charging
• (some of the) electricity has been generated using gas / coal / oil
Also accept: fossil fuels
AQA-8463.R_4_3_1_EQ_DENSITY

Write down the equation which links density (ρ), mass (m) and volume (V).

[1 mark]

• density = mass / volume
• or
• ρ = m / V
AQA-8463.R_4_2_4_EQ_ENERGY_POWER_TIME

Write down the equation which links energy (E), power (P) and time (t).

[1 mark]

• energy = power × time
• or
• E = P × t
AQA-8463.R_4_1_2_EQ_EFFICIENCY

Write down the equation which links efficiency, total energy input and useful energy output.

[1 mark]

• efficiency = useful energy output / total energy input
• or
• efficiency = useful output energy transfer / total input energy transfer
AQA-8463.R_4_5_2_EQ_WORK_DONE

Write down the equation which links distance (s), force (F) and work done (W).

[1 mark]

• work done = force × distance
• or
• W = Fs
Also accept: any correct rearrangement
AQA-8463.R_4_2_1_EQ_CHARGE_FLOW

Write down the equation which links charge flow (Q), current (I) and time (t).

[1 mark]

• charge flow = current × time
• or
• Q = It
AQA-8463.R_4_6_1_EQ_WAVE_SPEED

Write down the equation which links frequency (f), wave speed (v) and wavelength (λ).

[1 mark]

• wave speed = frequency × wavelength
• or
• v = f λ
Also accept: correct re-arrangement
AQA-8463.R_4_4_2_IRRADIATION_CONTAMINATION

People who work in the nuclear power industry need to be aware of irradiation and contamination. Describe the difference between irradiation and contamination.

[2 marks]

• irradiation is the exposure of an object / person to radiation
• (while) contamination is the (unwanted) presence of radioactive material / atoms on an object / person
Also accept: ‘absorption of radiation’ for ‘exposure’
Also accept: specific examples of ionising radiation
Also accept: ‘inside a person’ for ‘on an object / person’
AQA-8463.R_4_4_3_RADIATION_HEALTH_RISK

Give one health risk to a person working close to a source of nuclear radiation.

[1 mark]

any **one** from:
• cancer / tumours
• DNA / genetic mutation
• damages / kills cells
• radiation poisoning / sickness / burns
Ignore: mutates cells
Ignore: death
AQA-8463.R_4_1_3_CARBON_DIOXIDE_PROBLEM

Explain one environmental problem caused by the emission of carbon dioxide.

[2 marks]

• carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas
• (which) causes global warming
Also accept: carbon dioxide causes the greenhouse effect
Also accept: absorbs infrared (radiation)
Also accept: climate change
Also accept: examples of climate change eg sea levels rising, extreme weather conditions, etc
AQA-8463.R_4_4_3_MAN_MADE_BACKGROUND

Radioactive waste from nuclear power stations is a man-made source of background radiation. Give one other man-made source of background radiation.

[1 mark]

Any **one** from:
• (medical) x-rays
• radiotherapy
• nuclear weapons (testing)
• named nuclear disaster eg Chernobyl / Fukushima / Three Mile Island.
Also accept: CT scans
Also accept: nuclear fallout
Ignore: radioactive / nuclear waste
AQA-8463.R_4_8_1_OUR_GALAXY

What is the name of the galaxy our solar system is part of?

[1 mark]
Milky Way
AQA-8463.R_4_5_5_ATMOSPHERE_STATE

What state of matter is most of the Earth’s atmosphere?

[1 mark]
gas
AQA-8463.R_4_6_3_SUN_EARTH_INFRARED

The Sun and the Earth both emit infrared radiation. How does the rate of infrared radiation emitted by the Sun compare with the rate of infrared radiation emitted by the Earth? Give a reason for your answer.

[2 marks]

• greater rate than the Earth
• the Sun is at a higher temperature
Also accept: the Sun has a greater surface area
AQA-8463.R_4_8_2_BIG_BANG_START

The Big Bang theory is one model used to explain the origin of the universe. How does the Big Bang theory describe the universe when it began?

[1 mark]

(extremely) hot and dense
Ignore: very small
AQA-8463.R_4_5_6_BRAKING_DISTANCE_FACTORS

The braking distance of a car increases as the speed of the car increases. Give two other factors that increase the braking distance of a car.

[2 marks]

any **two** from:
• wet / icy road conditions
• poor condition of brakes
• poor condition of tyres
• increased mass of car
• negative gradient of the road
Also accept: weight for mass
Also accept: going downhill
Ignore: weather
AQA-8463.R_4_5_6_REACTION_TIME_THINKING

Explain why the driver’s reaction time affects the thinking distance of a car.

[2 marks]

• distance = speed × time
• (so) longer reaction time = longer distance
AQA-8463.R_4_8_1_SOLAR_SYSTEM_OBJECTS

The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system. Give three other types of object that form our solar system.

[3 marks]

• planets
• dwarf planets
• moons
• or
• natural satellites
Also accept: asteroids / meteors / meteoroids / meteorites
Also accept: comets
AQA-8463.R_4_6_2_RADIO_GAMMA_SIMILARITIES

Radio waves and gamma rays both transfer energy. Give three other similarities between radio waves and gamma rays.

[3 marks]

any **three** from:
• they travel at the same speed (in a vacuum / air)
• they can travel through a vacuum
• they are transverse (waves)
• they are electromagnetic (waves)
Also accept: they travel at the speed of light
Also accept: they do not need a medium (to travel)
Ignore: they can be reflected / refracted / absorbed / transmitted / diffracted.
AQA-8463.R_4_6_2_GAMMA_MEDICAL_USE

Both radio waves and gamma rays are used in medicine. Give one medical use of gamma rays.

[1 mark]

any **one** from:
• (medical) imaging
• (medical) treatments
Also accept: correctly named method eg PET scan, tracer, gamma camera
Also accept: correctly named treatment eg radiotherapy, brachiotherapy, gamma knife
Also accept: sterilising medical equipment
Not accepted: ultrasound, CT scan, X-rays, MRI scan
Not accepted: chemotherapy
AQA-8463.R_4_6_2_GAMMA_HARMFUL

Explain why exposure to gamma rays can be harmful but exposure to radio waves is not harmful.

[2 marks]

• gamma rays are (weakly) ionising but radio waves are **not** (ionising)
• (so gamma rays) can cause mutations in genes / DNA
• or
• (so gamma rays) can increase the risk of cancers
Also accept: can cause cancer
Also accept: damages / kills cells
AQA-8463.R_4_6_2_RADIO_WAVE_PRODUCTION

Some medical scanners produce radio waves at a specific frequency. Explain how radio waves are produced at a specific frequency.

[2 marks]

• (radio waves are produced by) oscillations in electrical circuits (of the scanner)
• the radio waves have the same frequency as the oscillations
Also accept: (radio waves are produced by) alternating current
Also accept: (radio waves are produced by) oscillating electrons (in an aerial)
AQA-8463.R_4_7_3_TRANSFORMER_SECONDARY_PD

There is an alternating current in the primary coil of a transformer. Explain why there is an alternating potential difference across the ends of the secondary coil of the transformer.

[3 marks]

• (the ac in the primary) causes a changing magnetic field in the core
• the secondary coil cuts through the (changing) magnetic field
• **inducing** a pd (across the ends of the secondary coil)
• or
• so a pd is **induced** (across the ends of the secondary coil)
AQA-8463.R_4_8_1_MAIN_SEQUENCE_STABLE

A main sequence star in a distant galaxy is the same size and mass as the Sun. Explain why the star is stable while it is in the main sequence stage of its life cycle.

[2 marks]

• gravitational force inwards and forces as a result of fusion reactions outwards
• are in equilibrium / balanced
Also accept: fusion energy for fusion reactions outwards
Also accept: radiation pressure for fusion reactions outwards
Also accept: for 1 mark forces are in equilibrium
AQA-8463.R_4_6_2_ULTRAVIOLET_USE

Ultraviolet is a type of electromagnetic wave. Give one use of ultraviolet.

[1 mark]

any **one** from:
• (sun) tan
• energy efficient lamps
Also accept: (invisible) security coding
Also accept: detecting forged bank notes
Also accept: kill microbes
Also accept: attract insects
Also accept: sterilise (surgical) equipment
Also accept: cause the body to produce vitamin D
Also accept: increasing the growth rate of plants
Also accept: water purification
